notes.title: Smasher 0.5.1 Update
notes.content:
This is just a tiny patch to make sure players don't see some things in the wrong order.

Bigger updates are in the works for later (but this little fix couldn't wait!).

notes.title: Smasher Alpha Update: Version 0.5.0
notes.content:
This update is a massive revision.

Let's start with the most significant change: Lives are now unlimited. The life limit was too punishing, and it detracted from more important aspects of the experience. This change also greatly expands the level design space, allowing more local difficulty and death.

Time boxes have been added, and the "Research" and "Slimed" episodes have been restructured to make use of them. This multi-timeline structure will be developed and expanded upon in future updates.

New enemies have been added. Make your way to the Crawler Lab and the Laser Lab (in the "Research" episode) to meet these new friends.

And then there are a plethora of other changes and improvements (such as improved movement, key handling, and digging). But let's not sit here and list them all—of course there are lots of changes during initial development. Go play the game already.

Enjoy!

notes.title: Smasher Alpha Update: Version 0.3.0
notes.content:
Smasher Alpha 0.3.0 is here!

And thanks to your helpful feedback, Smasher is better than ever.

There are too many changes to list (or read), but here's a summary of the important stuff:

[list]
[*]All five alpha episodes have been updated and revised.
[*]Episodes two (Research) and four (Slimed) have been almost fully redesigned using lots of exciting new material.
[*]A fun new piece is in the game, but I don't want to spoil it for you.
[*]Smasher's movement has been fine-tuned: Take off quicker, make tighter turns, and stop more easily.
[*]Timelines have been added to the pause screen. They show your progress through the episode.
[*]The display settings have a new rendering quality setting (low, high, and ultra), with a GPU probe to detect which to use (run automatically on first launch).
[*]Automatically recorded replays are now limited to the 200 most recent episode runs; older replays are deleted. This was unlimited before, which eventually causes problems. Copy an automatic replay to a named replay to keep it forever (except it might not play correctly in future Smasher updates—the game's still evolving, which can break a replay's determinism).
[*]GPU shaders are now all fully loaded on the initial launch screen, to prevent rare stutters on their first use.
[*]A number of sporadic and subtle audio pops and clicks have been fixed. This is thanks to my fancy new headphones and external DAC, which together produce a highly accurate frequency response (my speakers had been filtering these tiny bugs from my ears!).
[*]There's a bunch of other things, but go play the game already!
[/list]
Thank you all for your feedback. You are helping to make Smasher great.

Enjoy!
